evidence.ref: In-session resume is the WIRED DEFAULT of warp fleet. bin/warp cmd_fleet builds fleet.InSessionWaiter when no waiter is injected (bin/warp docstring + cmd_fleet body added in 70a9ecb), so a living fleet that has hit every account's budget waits until the governor's resume time and re-checks the desired count before spawning, never resuming straight into the limit and detaching nothing. The default path creates no timer and no background process.

selftest (WARP-0907, scripts/selftest.py ~5764-5794) drives cmd_fleet with waiter=None over a fake controller and a spy waiter and asserts: exactly one in-session default waiter is built when none is injected; the default waits until the governor resume epoch (4242) then re-checks; and a backed-off pool that then drains calls start zero times (spawns nothing). Runs over an injected clock so the gate never sleeps.

.warp/supervisor.py is OFF by default: importing the module and not calling install() creates no artifact, schedules nothing, and launches nothing; with no explicit warp supervisor install the fleet behaves exactly as the AC1 in-session default. The module reaches nothing on import (only the explicit supervisor subcommand path calls install/status/uninstall).

selftest (WARP-0907, scripts/selftest.py ~5814-5816) asserts no timer and no service unit exist until install() is explicitly called, over a temp unit dir. AC5 CLI check (~5895-5901) confirms warp supervisor with no action and warp supervisor install with no schedule both fail loud (nonzero) touching no systemd.

warp supervisor install generates a standard systemd user timer plus a oneshot service unit (supervisor.py timer_unit_text / service_unit_text: [Timer] OnCalendar + WantedBy=timers.target, [Service] Type=oneshot + ExecStart), with OnCalendar computed from the governor resume epoch (next_reset_calendar over governor.resume_at), enabled through an injected runner (systemctl user enable plus daemon-reload); it prints exactly what it created and is idempotent (deterministic unit bytes). warp supervisor status reports timer state and warp supervisor uninstall disables and removes both units cleanly. It is a user systemd timer a person inspects with systemctl user, not a system crontab, resident daemon, lock-refresher, or headless polling loop.

selftest (WARP-0907, scripts/selftest.py ~5810-5854) proves over a temp XDG dir and a FAKE systemctl: install generates the timer + oneshot service, computes OnCalendar from the resume epoch, enables via the injected runner and daemon-reload, is idempotent and confined (re-run writes identical bytes, exactly two units in the dir), status reports installed/is-enabled/is-active through the runner, and uninstall disables + removes both units and is idempotent (second removal is a clean no-op). The gate never touches the real user systemd.

The session-launch primitive is a fail-loud reference seam: supervisor.launch_session raises SupervisorLaunchError when no real launcher is wired (the same honesty shape as fleet.in_session_start) and delegates to an injected launcher when one is provided. WARP generates the timer and the documented ExecStart launch command but never spawns a session itself, in the gate, on the default path, or as a side effect of install. The only thing the opt-in path creates is an inert, inspectable systemd user unit the OS scheduler runs at the reset time. supervisor.py imports no subprocess at module top and never calls os.fork or os.system; RealSystemctl lazily imports subprocess only to run systemctl.

selftest (WARP-0907, scripts/selftest.py ~5830-5890) asserts install runs only systemctl subcommands (daemon-reload/enable/disable/is-enabled/is-active) and launches no session; launch_session fails loud unwired and delegates when wired; a fabricate-a-schedule install (no resume_at, no on_calendar) is refused (RULE #6); and a launch spy proves install never calls launch_session by default or as a side effect.

.warp/supervisor.py ships in the canonical engine (plugin/templates/.warp/supervisor.py) and all seven packs re-synced byte-identical (content and mode); the bin/warp supervisor subcommand ships identically across the engine and packs (100755). Three new capabilities.yaml entries are honest and NOT marked repo-only because they ship: fleet_in_session_resume_default (mechanical, home bin/warp + .warp/fleet.py), fleet_external_supervisor (mechanical, home .warp/supervisor.py + bin/warp), and fleet_supervisor_session_launch (reference, home .warp/supervisor.py); they pass the WARP-0906 home-resolution honesty check. Both capabilities.yaml copies stay byte-identical. docs/runbook.md (version 1.5 to 1.6) documents the in-session default and the opt-in external supervisor: that it is off by default, how to enable, inspect, and remove it, and the no-detached-process boundary.

selftest (WARP-0907, scripts/selftest.py ~5895-5903) confirms bin/warp routes supervisor to supervisor.py and it fails loud without touching real systemd, and that .warp/supervisor.py resolves in the shipped engine (in _CH_ENGINE), so the WARP-0906 honesty check treats the new entries as shipped, not repo-only. Gate check_pack_drift reports empty for all seven packs and cross-pack conformance passes, proving the engine and pack copies are byte-identical.

The selftest includes the supervisor tests, the capabilities-honesty check, the pack drift check, and cross-pack conformance across all seven packs. No protected path is edited (scripts/verify.sh, scripts/warp-guard.sh, .warp/policy.yaml, .warp/policy_check.py or their plugin/templates twins); the index is regenerated; RULE #1 is clean (no em/en dash, every double-hyphen a real systemd or CLI flag); and the warp name is unchanged.
